note: Ozarks ranch campground near Bunker, with the Mark Twain National Forest on three sides: one row of 20 long gravel back-in pads along spring-fed Sinking Creek, facing open pasture, plus glamping tents and creekside tent sites. Private dirt-bike and side-by-side trails start at the pads and riders are common. Horses by arrangement. Little cell service. The operator warns trailers off Highway A: come in on Highway 72 or 19. --Claude

Passes the $50 gate at the posted rate (Friday $54.24 with tax). Google 4.8 over 33. The stored note's 'weekend stays need both nights' was wrong for RV sites and is dropped. Pads still cannot be seen on imagery.
flags: NOTE CORRECTION: the stored note and inclusion evidence say weekend stays need both nights. On the operator's site that sentence belongs to the 'Weekday Escape' glamping-tent offer ('Weekend stays need both Friday and Saturday'). A one-night Friday RV booking (2027-06-18) went into the ResNexus cart at $50.00, so RV sites carry no minimum. Removed from the note.

PRICE GATE: $50.00 Fri/Sat before tax, $54.24 with the 8.475% tax; $40.00 / $43.39 on the other five nights. Nothing mandatory is added (no per-person, vehicle, pet or resort fee; travel protection is optional). At the gate, not over it, on the published rate - stays. gateways.py not needed.

QUALITY: Google 4.8 over 33 reviews (was 27 on 2026-10-03). The operator's own page quotes 4.86 over 44 on Airbnb and 22 Hipcamp reviews. Long-stay: weekly and monthly rates are offered ($600 a month) but the 20 pads are all sold nightly online, 13 of 15 hookup pads open tonight and 14 in June 2027 - no sign of resident occupancy.

QUESTION FOR THE OWNER (off-road rule): the RV page now sells the place to riders - 'Wake up at the trailhead', 'Unload the machines and ride straight into the national forest', '7+ miles of single track for dirt bikes', '4.5 mile loop for side by sides and four wheelers' on the ranch, 'Daylight riding only'. It is still a general campground (glamping tents, horses, tent sites, anyone may book) and was kept on 2026-10-03 as 'a general campground near forest trails, not an OHV park'; the riding is on the campground's own land, though, so it is closer to an OHV-side campground than that line suggests. Kept with the riding stated in the note; drop if that reads as an off-road park.

PIN (flag, cannot be fixed from imagery): stored 37.4893,-91.3076 sits on County Road 5615 in woods, about 300 m west of the ranch buildings. Google's place point is 37.48967,-91.30245 (460 m east of the stored pin, on the county road at the pasture gate). Esri imagery still predates the campground: it shows the farm buildings at about 37.4901,-91.3043, the long hay pasture east of them and the creek's tree line along the pasture's north-east edge, but no gravel drive or pads. The operator's map describes 'one gravel drive in, one row of sites along the creek' with 'open pasture across the drive'. Suggest moving the pin to Google's point 37.48967,-91.30245 as the nearest confirmed point of the property; the pad row itself is unlocated.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront; operator claim differs, gate re-run, no change): the operator says 'Creekside pads' and every ResNexus unit text says 'The pad backs up to the creek'. Imagery cannot confirm - no pads are visible, and the creek corridor is a continuous tree line, so a pad backing onto it would be behind trees, not on an open apron. Sinking Creek here is a small spring-fed stream. Stays down; recheck when imagery shows the pads.
